_about: Per phase: which capability slots to consider, when, and why. need: core = use unless you can state a reason not to; situational = use only when the condition holds; optional = only if it clearly helps. The conductor decides each one and records it with `hyperskill.py skills use|skip`.

research.when: at the start, before the interview, whenever the market or alternatives are not already documented
research.why: a multi-source sweep gives docs/research.md evidence instead of guesses

research.when: only if the idea is still vague after the first pass
research.why: pressure-tests the problem statement before any design is spent on it

research.when: only when a competitor or demo video is part of the evidence
research.why: turns a video into frames and a transcript you can cite

research.when: when the go/no-go rests on what real people say, and the first sweep leaves demand evidence thin
research.why: recent, cited threads and comments give the user-evidence check something real to point at

research.when: only to collect public data in bulk (pricing pages, listings) that WebFetch cannot gather one page at a time
research.why: structured competitor data for the alternatives-mapped check, within each site's terms

plan.when: when docs/system-design.md is written, before the user is asked to read it
plan.why: the system-design-read and architecture-explained checks need a diagram the user can follow and question

plan.when: from the first line of code onward; on by default
plan.why: small, surgical diffs and stated success checks stop the usual over-building

plan.when: after the design is drafted, if a second opinion is wanted
plan.why: extra reviewers on the architecture; hs-reviewer already stress-tests it

plan.when: only when the plan has to pick a component library
plan.why: evidence for the library decision, recorded with `decide`

plan.when: only if the product is a standard site (landing, sign-in, dashboard) and the stack is not fixed yet
plan.why: a generated, browser-tested starting point saves the foundation work, but it must be chosen before the stack

plan.when: when an idea in the design (cache key, queue, auth flow) is hard to explain in words
plan.why: an interactive figure makes the architecture review concrete

foundation.when: for every change set, before and while writing it
foundation.why: keeps migrations, auth and tenancy code minimal and reviewable

an independent read catches missing tenant scoping and validation; with Open Code Review switched on and its `ocr` CLI installed, use its delegate skill as a second, rules-based flaw hunt (Claude reviews, no extra key) and record its findings in docs/reviews/

foundation.when: when the build steps are large enough to need TDD and sub-plans
foundation.why: structure inside a phase; it never replaces HyperSkill's gates

product.when: before any pixels, once per project (one design voice only)
product.why: sets the look and dials so the UI is a decision, not a default

product.when: instead of design-direction when you want generated tokens and font pairing (not both)
product.why: tokens, palette and type from local data feed the design system

product.when: before designing, if real-product references would help (hosted, inspiration only)
product.why: reference screens widen the options; never copy them

product.when: when the UI needs an icon set
product.why: one collection, one licence, recorded for the icon-set-licence gate

product.when: after the UI works, only where motion explains something
product.why: motion craft and a motion audit, without decorative animation

product.when: once the screens exist, before the designer-pass gate
product.why: anti-pattern detection and critique, written to docs/design-audit.md

product.when: after every UI change that matters
product.why: drives the real UI at phone and desktop widths and shows screenshots as evidence

product.when: before the a11y gates are marked passed
product.why: automated accessibility findings with real selectors

product.when: when the UI, README or landing has written copy
product.why: flags AI-sounding text; claims must still be true

product.when: only if the site was scaffolded in plan, or the project is a standard site and the stack allows it
product.why: generates pages, API routes and browser checks from one config

product.when: for build steps large enough to need a plan, tests first and sub-steps
product.why: TDD and bite-sized plans inside the phase

product.when: when the product page or docs need an interactive explainer
product.why: a crafted figure explains an idea better than a screenshot

product.when: after the pages are built and before the design critique, when node is installed
product.why: a mechanical check of the built HTML and CSS against anti-slop rules, so the critique spends its time on judgement

ship.when: on every change set going to main
ship.why: the independent review the ship gates rely on; with Open Code Review switched on and its `ocr` CLI installed, use its delegate skill as a second, rules-based flaw hunt (Claude reviews, no extra key) and record its findings in docs/reviews/

ship.when: for end-to-end exploration beyond the scripted e2e tests
ship.why: finds what scripted tests were not written to look for

ship.when: on the preview deployment before release
ship.why: proves the deployed page works in a real browser

ship.when: only if its flow respects the CI and CD gates
ship.why: automates the PR and deploy steps; the gates still win

ship.when: for fixes large enough to need a written plan and tests first

harden.when: for the independent review, run by hs-reviewer in a sandbox
harden.why: findings with evidence go to docs/security/ and become regression tests

harden.when: on the diff of every security fix
harden.why: fixes are code too and need review; with Open Code Review switched on and its `ocr` CLI installed, use its delegate skill as a second, rules-based flaw hunt (Claude reviews, no extra key) and record its findings in docs/reviews/

harden.when: when the product ships a bundle or binary to users' machines (a web build, Electron app, mobile app)
harden.why: what you ship is what an attacker reads: leaked secrets, published source maps and unexpected endpoints

operate.when: right after a deploy, if a canary tool is installed
when response times or page weight look wrong

launch.when: only if the launch needs a promo or demo video
launch.why: renders a video from a brief; our video file supplies brief and verification

launch.when: only with a video that has speech
only with a video that needs titles or callouts
only with written consent for any cloned voice
launch.why: synthetic voice for narration; must be disclosed

launch.when: to verify your own rendered video
launch.why: frames and transcript prove the render says what the brief says

launch.when: on the launch copy, README and landing text
launch.why: claims must be true and the text must not read as generated

launch.when: only for a missing landing or download page on a standard site
launch.why: generates the page and tests it in a browser

launch.when: when the launch page needs one memorable explainer

scale.when: to find the real bottleneck before optimising
for load tests or several instances at once
at the end of the project
for the post-launch backlog, one agent per task
scale.why: every output still goes through gates and review
